abstract: Methamphetamine (METH) is highly addictive, and can cause neurotoxicity when misused over a prolonged period. METH-induced neurotoxicity and addiction involve multi-level biological alterations, including genetic susceptibility, aberrant epigenetic modifications, transcriptional imbalance, protein dysfunction, metabolic dysregulation, and microbial dysbiosis with changes in microbiota-derived metabolites. To systematically dissect these changes, genomics has been deployed to identify key gene polymorphisms linked to METH addiction susceptibility and epigenetic changes such as DNA methylation in brain regions following METH exposure. Transcriptomics dynamically profiles differential gene expression in addiction-relevant brain areas, particularly in pathways governing synaptic plasticity and neuroinflammation. Proteomics pinpoints the dysregulation of functional proteins associated with synaptic plasticity in response to METH. Metabolomics quantifies neurotransmitter depletion and redox imbalance induced by the drug. Microbiomics reveals gut microbiota dysbiosis and subsequent neural damage via the brain-gut axis. This review summarizes the applications of omics analysis technologies in METH neurotoxicity and addiction research, aiming to provide a reference for elucidating pathogenic mechanisms, identifying biomarkers, and discovering potential therapeutic targets.

Language="chi"><AbstractText>甲基苯丙胺（METH）具有高度成瘾性，长期滥用可导致神经毒性。METH诱导的神经毒性及成瘾涉及遗传易感性、表观遗传修饰异常、转录失衡、蛋白质功能紊乱、代谢稳态失调以及微生物及其衍生物紊乱等多个层面。为系统解析上述多层次改变，基因组学鉴定了与METH成瘾易感性相关的关键基因多态性及METH暴露后脑区DNA甲基化等表观遗传改变;转录组学动态刻画了METH处理后相关脑区中突触可塑性、神经炎症通路的差异表达基因谱;蛋白质组学精准定位了METH引起的与突触可塑性相关的功能蛋白表达失调;代谢组学量化了METH诱导的神经递质耗竭和氧化还原失衡;微生物组学则揭示了METH暴露导致肠道菌群紊乱，并通过脑-肠轴介导神经系统损害。本文综述了组学分析技术在METH神经毒性和成瘾研究中的应用现状，以期为阐明METH滥用的致病机制、筛选生物标志物和发掘潜在治疗靶点提供参考。.</AbstractText></OtherAbstract><KeywordList
